threadListItem.$description: The Message Center thread-list row — SINCE 2026-07-24 THE INBOX SHAPE IS THE ONLY SHAPE. The original card/metadata-row shape (subject + chevron + Department/Received label:value rows, built on Card's interactive shell with a build-time assertion against Card's real tokens) was removed per explicit request once the inbox redesign fully replaced it in the prototype — see decision-log 2026-07-24 for its history. What remains: a full-bleed flat row (avatar + identity + timestamp + subject + preview + flag toggle + optional Expires badge) with required unread/read states — see the inbox group below for all of it.

inbox.$description: The Message Center inbox-list row layout (avatar + department identity + timestamp + subject + preview + flag + optional Expires) — the component's only shape since the card/metadata-row shape was removed 2026-07-24. Avatar is a real Avatar (resolved from avatar.tokens.json — SM size, 32px, since 2026-07-24 feedback; was base/40px), keyed off the department name (not a person) — same fallback-color hashing logic, just fed a department string instead of a person's name, so 'Academic Advising' always lands on the same identity color. No 'Handled by' row and no right-aligned Expires column (both present in the live inbox screenshot) — deliberately dropped/repositioned per explicit request: Expires moves to a left-aligned row directly under the preview text instead. REDESIGNED 2026-07-24 per explicit feedback, following the staff-mockup reference: not a rounded, bordered card sitting in a padded/gapped list — inbox rows are FULL-BLEED flat rows (no radius, no own border, no gaps) separated by a 1px list.divider, filling the rail edge to edge. Every row is in one of two required states: 'unread' (whiter, higher contrast, heavier weights) or 'read' (grayer, lower contrast, normal weights) — see those groups below. Because a flat row has no border to color, hover/pressed use the ghost fill.neutralHover/fill.neutralActive convention (list.hoverBg/list.activeBg); 'selected' is the persistent state.selected.bg fill.

identitySecondary.$description: Mixed-sender support, added 2026-07-26 from client feedback (department-only senders feel impersonal — students build relationships with individual advisors too). When a thread's sender is a person, the identity line renders 'Person Name · Department': the name keeps inbox.identity's own styling and THIS group styles the ' · Department' suffix — normal weight, muted color, same size — so the person carries the line and the department quietly contextualizes it. Announcement threads keep the department alone as the sender. The avatar keys off whichever name leads the line (person or department), via Avatar's usual hashing.

reply.$description: Replyability indicator on the preview line, added 2026-07-26 from client feedback (users want to know whether a message accepts replies BEFORE opening it). v2 same day, per explicit feedback ('the gray icon reads unclear'): the muted reply ICON was replaced by a REAL BADGE — sm (16px), role=success, tint (pale green bg + active green text), label 'Replied' — resolved from badge.tokens.json exactly like the Expires badge; this group keeps no tokens of its own anymore. Badge present = replies allowed; absent = announcement / replies closed; the preview simply crops earlier. The same fact shows inside the thread view as the Composer being replaced by a quiet closed-replies hint (EmptyState's pill recipe).

flag.$description: 2026-07-24: the flag became a real, clickable per-thread toggle (student marks a thread important), not a static staff-side glyph. Unflagged = the OUTLINED flag icon (assets/icons/material-outlined/flag.svg — first outlined icon in the repo, sourced 2026-07-24) in icon.muted; flagged = the FILLED flag (material-filled/flag.svg) in icon.warning (yellow). Because the row now contains a nested interactive element, the inbox row is a <div role='button' tabindex='0'> with a real nested <button> for the flag — the same no-interactive-inside-interactive resolution Attachment's idle shape already established (a real <button> can't nest another one).

list.$description: The full-bleed list presentation: rows separated by a 1px divider, no per-row radius/border/gaps. Hover/pressed reuse the established ghost progression (transparent-ish rest → fill.neutralHover → fill.neutralActive) because a flat borderless row has nothing for the card shell's blue hover border to attach to.

unread.$description: A thread with activity the viewer hasn't opened yet — whiter and higher-contrast than 'read': surface.default bg, text.default identity/subject at weight.semibold, preview one step darker (text.secondary) than read's. Identity/subject keep their shared base typography (size/leading) from inbox.identity / threadListItem.subject — only weight and color swap per state.

read.$description: Already-opened thread — grayer and lower-contrast: surface.dim bg (2026-07-24: first tried surface.page — literally white, dims nothing — then surface.sunken/gray.100, which explicit feedback called too heavy next to unread's white; surface.dim/gray.50 was added to the semantic layer for exactly this), text.secondary identity/subject at weight.normal, text.muted preview.

selected.$description: Persistent bg.primary fill for the thread currently open in the reading pane — the meaning survives from the original Card-interactive shell even though the card shape itself is gone (2026-07-24): a selected row is 'as if permanently pressed'.
